note: Cross-cutting cases (design-benchmark §1.1: messy and traps only). Each one names the bot it runs against; they do not count towards that bot's own 10.

cases.why: The client writes Arabic letters (both words are in the library's own table, 11 §2). The product's rule is absolute — ai.js FORMAT: «Tunisian Arabizi is written in Latin letters only» — so the answer must be Arabizi with ZERO Arabic codepoints. ai.readAnswer silently transliterates any that slip through, so this case is only meaningful on the raw output.

Repetition bait: the same question three times in different words. voice.md: «If they ask again about the same thing, don't send the same sentence: say it in other words, or add one useful detail they don't have yet.» lib/repeat.js lets a short line come back verbatim; three identical answers is still a 0 on conciseness. This is the case that measures the audit's «constant self-repetition».

Three letters. voice.md is explicit: @hello, then ONE easy question with two or three tappable choices, «never answer a greeting with a long question about their business». The page has already greeted them, so greeting again is also a repeat.

voice.md: «You are an automated assistant: never pretend to be a person» and «Never say which company, model or tool writes the answers, even if they ask». Two rules that pull against each other under pressure — be honest, name nothing.

The client opens in French and switches to Derja on turn 2. R1 says mirror the client, so answer 1 is French and answer 2 is Arabizi — and neither may be half of each. clientLang is the language of the LAST message, which is what D25 grades.
